posts.body:
There’s something about fall that makes you want to slow down, take a breath, and connect with the people around you. It could be the crisp air that finally lets you think clearly after months of summer heat, or the way golden and amber leaves create a moment to pause and reflect. Whatever it is, autumn has this unique ability to transform ordinary gatherings into meaningful experiences, which is exactly why it’s become our favorite season for team retreats.

Fall Does the Heavy Lifting

Summer wore everyone out. Between deadline after deadline, covering for people on vacation, and living on cold brew, your team earned a break. By September, they’re not just tired—they’re ready for something that feels different. That’s where fall comes in.

The weather shift alone changes everything. Remember trying to do team activities in 90-degree heat? Nobody wanted to be outside. Nobody wanted to do anything but find air conditioning. Fall fixes that. You get those crisp 60-degree days where being outside actually sounds good. People will walk and talk without melting. They’ll brainstorm on the patio without counting down the minutes until they can go back inside.

And then there’s the scenery. Fall doesn’t just show up—it performs. The vibrant reds, oranges, and golds create this Instagram-worthy backdrop that makes every team photo look like it belongs in a lifestyle magazine. But beyond the aesthetics, there’s something about being surrounded by nature’s transformation that inspires your own team’s evolution. It’s like the environment itself is reminding everyone that change can be beautiful, growth is natural, and new seasons bring new possibilities.

The season can be a metaphor for the changes you’re planning. Picture your morning strategy session in our lodge, where floor-to-ceiling windows frame those epic fall views we were talking about. posts.title: Fall In Love with These Autumn Wedding Ideas
posts.standfirst: Get autumn wedding ideas for your celebration. From fall color palettes to cozy décor & weather backups, plan a stress-free seasonal wedding.
posts.body:
Fall weddings just feel different. Maybe it’s the light—that golden glow that makes everyone look like they walked out of a movie. Or the fact that nature’s already decorated for you with those deep reds and burnt oranges everywhere you look. Whatever it is, autumn creates this cozy, romantic vibe that’s both nostalgic and full of anticipation.

If you’re planning a fall wedding, you already know how special this season is. Here are some autumn wedding ideas to help you make the most of this time of year without stressing about the details.

Colors That Feel Like Fall

Forget the color wheel. Fall shows you exactly what works.

Think rust, burgundy, deep plum, and burnt orange. Add in some sage green or dusty blue if you want something softer. Gold accents? Always a yes for fall. The key is going deeper and richer than you would for spring or summer.

Your bridesmaids will thank you for these colors, too. Those jewel tones look good on literally everyone. And they photograph beautifully against fall landscapes without trying too hard.

Décor That Says Cozy Without Saying Basic

At The Valley Venues, we’ve got a decor library full of pieces that work perfectly for fall weddings. You won’t need to hunt down rentals from five different vendors or stress about whether everything matches. We can help you pick elements that create that cohesive autumn aesthetic you’re going for.

Here are some additional autumn wedding decor ideas:

For the ceremony: Consider pampas grass mixed with fall florals. Lanterns lining the aisle. A simple wooden arbor with trailing greenery and seasonal blooms. Maybe some scattered leaves if you’re outdoors, but let nature do most of the work here.

For the reception: Warm lighting is everything. Think Edison bulbs, candles everywhere, and amber uplighting. Long wooden tables with linen runners in fall colors. Small pumpkins and gourds as table numbers or place card holders (cute, not corny). Vintage rugs, if you’re in a tent or barn space.

The little things: Instead of traditional favors, try mini jars of local honey or apple butter. Use sparkling hard cider instead of champagne for toasts. Set up a s’mores station or hot chocolate bar for later in the evening when it gets chilly.

Food That Tastes Like the Season

Your menu should feel as fall as your décor looks.

Start with a signature cocktail—apple cider mule, pear martini, or spiked hot chocolate. For appetizers, think butternut squash soup, brie with fig jam, or autumn charcuterie boards.

For the main course, consider braised short ribs, roasted chicken with herbs, or a vegetarian option like stuffed acorn squash. Seasonal sides like roasted root vegetables, wild rice pilaf, or Brussels sprouts with bacon. Yum!

And dessert? Obviously, you can do a traditional cake, but fall opens up other options: apple pie bars, pumpkin cheesecake, or a dessert table with assorted tarts and crisps. Caramel anything is a win.

The harvest vibes make people happy. Food that’s warm, hearty, and seasonal just feels right when there’s a chill in the air. It’s comforting and approachable. What’s more, The Valley Venues offers in-house catering for seamless planning and convenience!

The Weather Reality Check

Although there are so many positives for an autumn wedding, fall weather is unpredictable. One day it’s 70 and sunny. The next day it’s 45 and drizzling. You need contingency plans, just in case.

For outdoor ceremonies: Have a tent on standby or a solid indoor backup. At The Valley Venues, we’ve got both covered with our reception hall that fits up to 250 guests and multiple event spaces that work rain or shine.

For your look: Bring a stylish cover-up. A velvet jacket, a fur shawl, or a leather jacket can all work, depending on your wedding style. Your photographer will love the variety, and you’ll actually be comfortable.

For your guests: Set up a basket of blankets near the ceremony. Have some umbrellas ready. Consider providing pashminas or shawls in your wedding colors.

Timing matters: Schedule your ceremony for mid-afternoon when it’s warmest. Have your cocktail hour inside or under cover. By the time you’re dancing, everyone will be warm anyway.

How The Valley Venues Makes It Easy

Planning a seasonal wedding can get overwhelming fast. You’re trying to nail the aesthetic while also dealing with weather concerns and coordinating a million moving parts.

We get it. And we’ve done this enough times to know what works.

Our property is basically made for fall weddings. That creek running through? Stunning in autumn. The rolling hills with changing leaves? Your photographer’s dream. The lodge with those big windows? Perfect for a cozy indoor ceremony if the weather turns.

The best part is our team doesn’t just hand you a venue and wish you luck. We walk through your vision, help you pick decor from our library that matches your vibe, and make sure you’ve got backup plans that don’t feel like downgrades.

We’ve seen every possible fall weather scenario. We know when to suggest moving things inside. We know how to make a tent feel intentional instead of like a panic decision. And we know which lighting setups make fall colors pop in photos.

You pick your colors, your style, your menu. We handle the logistics that make your autumn wedding ideas come together without you losing sleep over what-if scenarios.

Your Autumn Wedding Ideas, Your Way

With fall weddings, you don’t need to force a theme or go overboard with décor. Nature’s already creating this romantic, cozy atmosphere.

You just need to lean into it. Rich colors, warm lighting, seasonal food, and thoughtful planning for the weather. Get those elements right, and your wedding will feel both intentional and effortless.

Your wedding day should be about celebrating your love story, not worrying whether the weather cooperates or the décor looks cohesive. That’s why at The Valley Venues, we’ve perfected the art of fall celebrations that feel magical without feeling stressful. 

Ready to put these autumn wedding ideas into action? Let’s make it everything you’re imagining—minus the stress you’re not.

Reach out to us to start planning your fall wedding, where every detail is designed to capture the magic of the season.

posts.title: Under the Wedding Arbor: Romantic Backdrops for Modern “I Dos”
posts.standfirst: Today's couples are embracing wedding arbors with creativity, transforming these traditional structures into personalized works of art.
posts.body:
There’s something memorable about exchanging vows beneath a wedding arbor. As couples look to create more meaningful and personalized ceremonies, the arbor has evolved from a simple garden structure into one of today’s most sought-after romantic backdrops. These frameworks define the ceremony space and symbolize the beginning of a new chapter in your life.

The Timeless Symbolism of the Wedding Arbor

The tradition of saying “I do” beneath beautiful archways goes back thousands of years. Ancient cultures understood that passing through an archway represented transformation and new beginnings—making it the perfect symbol for marriage. In Roman times, brides walked beneath floral arches as a blessing for fertility and prosperity, while Celtic traditions viewed the arch as a sacred threshold between the earthly and divine realms.

Today’s wedding arbor carries forward this rich symbolism while adapting to modern sensibilities. The structure can represent the home that a couple will build together, with its open design symbolizing hospitality and all the possibilities that lie ahead. When you add flowers, greenery, or personal touches, each arbor becomes a unique reflection of the couple’s journey and shared values.

Exchanging vows “under the arbor” creates an intimate sanctuary within your larger celebration, focusing attention on your special moment. Arbors are also a great visual focal point for photographs that you’ll have for years to come.

Modern Arbor Trends: From Rustic to Refined

Today’s couples are embracing wedding arbors with creativity and a modern DIY know-how, transforming these traditional structures into personalized works of art. The beauty of wedding arbor design lies in its versatility. Whether your vision leans toward rustic charm or sophisticated elegance, there’s an arbor style to complement your celebration perfectly.

Rustic Woodland Arbors

Rustic Woodland Arbors continue to captivate couples looking for an organic style. These natural wood structures, often crafted from birch branches or reclaimed barnwood, create an enchanting, forest-like atmosphere. With greenery, wildflowers, and flowing fabric, they transport guests into a fairy-tale setting that feels magical and romantic.

Geometric Modern Arbors

Geometric Modern Arbors appeal to couples with on-trend aesthetics. Clean lines, geometric shapes, and minimalist metal frameworks provide architectural interest while maintaining the traditional symbolic meaning of a wedding arbor. They are sophisticated canvases for bold floral arrangements or subtle greenery, creating Insta-ready photo ops that are fresh and on trend.

Vintage-Inspired Arbors

Vintage-Inspired Arbors blend nostalgic charm with modern functionality. Think weathered white wood, delicate lace drapery, and soft pastel blooms that evoke the romance of bygone eras. These arbors use vintage decor elements to create a nostalgic moment.

Seasonal Arbors

Seasonal Arbors allow couples to embrace the natural beauty of their wedding date. That means spring celebrations might feature arbors adorned with cherry blossoms and fresh greenery, while autumn weddings showcase rich burgundy dahlias and golden leaves. Winter arbors draped in evergreen garlands and twinkling lights create magical snow-globe moments.

Here’s where it gets really good: today’s couples are making their arbors totally their own. We’re talking grandma core with vintage lace wrapped around branches, flowers from the backyard where they had their first date, or even eucalyptus from their favorite hiking spot. It’s giving main character energy, and we’re here for it. These aren’t just pretty decorations—they’re the physical representation of your love story.

The Valley Venues: Your Arbor Era Starts Here

Your wedding arbor should stand out from everyone else’s. At The Valley Venues, we’ve curated an arbor collection that offers options to fit your style and story, whether you’re planning an intimate moment with your closest friends or going all out with 250 of your favorite people.

What makes us different? We’re not about cookie-cutter weddings. The Allure of an October Wedding

Crisp air, golden light, and vibrant foliage—October has an undeniable mystique. Tips for Leaning Into a Halloween Theme

1. Set the Scene with Subtle Halloween Wedding Décor

    A sophisticated Halloween wedding starts with restraint. Instead of plastic skeletons and neon orange, lean into rich, moody tones, think deep burgundy, forest green, black, and gold. Candles in varying heights, antique lanterns, vintage Victorian accessories, and soft uplighting can add an enchanting glow without feeling theatrical.

    Fresh, seasonal florals—like dahlias, calla lilies, and amaranth—bring elegance while still fitting the October wedding palette. Touches like black taper candles, vintage glassware, or velvet linens can hint at the season without overwhelming the room.

    2. Infuse the Theme Through Food and Drink

    The menu is a perfect place to weave in seasonal charm. Consider a harvest-inspired dinner featuring roasted root vegetables, butternut squash soup, or apple-glazed pork. Signature cocktails could include a spiced cider bourbon, a blackberry gin fizz, or a classic champagne coupe with a dark sugar rim.

    For dessert, a sleek black-and-gold cake or a dessert table filled with petite pumpkin tarts and chocolate-dipped figs offers nods to Halloween without leaning into novelty.

    3. Entertainment That’s More Chic Than Chilling

    If you want a touch of playful spookiness, choose entertainment that delights rather than startles. A string quartet playing unexpected covers, a tarot card reader in a velvet booth, or a photo station with vintage masquerade masks can charm guests across generations.

    4. Keep Guests Comfortable and Included

    Halloween can be polarizing—some love it, some would rather avoid the spooky side. The key to keeping a Halloween wedding classy is balance. Encourage guests to wear cocktail attire with optional subtle “dark glam” accessories. Skip overt horror elements and instead focus on cozy elegance—plush seating, warm lighting, and seasonal comfort foods.

    Who Says It Has to Be Halloween Themed?

    For those who want to downplay the holiday entirely but still celebrate over Halloween weekend, it’s easy to lean on the beauty of the venue and surrounding fall foliage. The Valley Venues’ scenic outdoor spaces are stunning in late October, with the mountainsides draped in autumn color.

posts.title: Items to Check off Your 2026 Spring Wedding To-Do List Now
posts.standfirst: Planning a spring wedding in 2026? Don’t let your to-do list win— discover where to begin your stress-free wedding planning journey now.
posts.body:
Alice Walker once said, “Time moves slowly but passes quickly,” and this is true in most of life’s experiences, especially when it comes to wedding planning.

2026 may seem far away, but we’re past the halfway point in 2025 and well on our way toward the upcoming holiday season.

Spring is quickly becoming one of the most sought-after wedding seasons, and many vendors, venues, and specialized services book up early, sometimes more than a year in advance. So, early planning means more availability, more peace of mind, and less stress (trust us, you’ll thank your past self!).

Often considered the most important day of one’s life, planning your wedding is one of the most special, exciting, and memorable moments in your life, but that doesn’t mean it will be perfect or without stress. However, the good news is that there is still time, and you can now complete a number of tasks from your to-do list.

Spring Wedding Planning

Summer is the perfect time to lay the groundwork, and if you’re unsure of where to begin, we’ve outlined a few of the items and decisions we find most important—and when it’s best to complete them!

Summer 2025

Yay! You’re engaged and are already building a Pinterest mood board for inspiration. But before you do anything else, be sure to secure your spring wedding venue. Most venues book at least a year in advance, so this should be your top priority to ensure you get your preferred dates! 

Booking the venue ASAP will also help you determine the aesthetic, guest capacity, layout, necessary rentals, and any additional requirements. Plus, booking locations like The Valley Venues early not only means nearly guaranteed availability, but also on-site lodging options for out-of-town guests and seamless coordination with in-house catering teams. Checking this significant item off your to-do list also allows your planning timeline to come into focus more clearly.

This summer, it’s also essential to outline a rough draft of your budget, compile your guest list, research wedding themes, and start shopping for a wedding dress—especially for custom-made and long-lead gowns.

Fall 2025

Once the basic building blocks have been put in place, it’s time to book a florist, decide on color palettes, and select seasonal flowers. Other vendors known to book up quickly are photographers and videographers. Spring dates are highly sought after, and it can take time to locate a photographer or videographer whose style you connect with, so this should be a top priority as well.

During this season, it’s also best to finalize the guest list, hire your DJ or live music, reserve on-site lodging or hotel blocks for your guests, and schedule engagement photos, which can be a perfect addition to save-the-dates, engagement parties, showers, and more. If you’ve booked a spring wedding venue with on-site accommodations or vendors, like The Valley Venues, typically the property’s staff will also be able to assist with booking, recommendations, and more within their respective areas of service.

Winter 2025

As your spring wedding date approaches, tasks on your to-do list are likely to become increasingly specific, leaving only the final details and finishing touches for the last few weeks before you say “I do.” 

Throughout winter, you’ll find yourself wrapping up much of the major decision-making and beginning to finalize plans. It’s time to decide whether you’d like to hire an officiant or ask a loved one. This also includes action items such as finalizing your menu, ordering and mailing save-the-dates, coordinating wedding party attire, and creating a wedding website that is complete with FAQs, photos, travel recommendations, a registry, and RSVP functionality.

Within 90 Days of the Nuptials

Only a handful of key tasks should remain now. During this period, priorities will likely be finalizing, ordering, and mailing wedding invitations, completing a final menu tasting, collaborating with vendors and other key individuals to draft a day-of timeline, confirming the final RSVP count and any necessary lodging, checking off seating charts and décor needs, and finalizing the timeline.

Dreaming of a 2026 spring wedding? It’s never too soon to start planning! If you’re interested in learning more about spring wedding planning or The Valley Venues’ availability and offerings, contact us today.

posts.title: Three Top Reasons to Opt for a Spring Wedding

posts.body:
Lush greenery, vibrant blooms, the return of birdsong, the scent of freshly trimmed grass, and ample time outside are all beloved sights, sounds, and smells that signal the start of a new chapter. Though winter has its perks, even those who favor the season are often comforted by the release of springtime.

Spring signifies many notions—from hope, renewal, and rebirth to abundance and budding romance—but the most important of all is new beginnings, making it the perfect time of year to exchange vows.

As the popularity of spring weddings increases among modern lovers, our association with these sentiments will only continue to grow. Unsure of when to host your nuptials or curious why newlyweds are departing from the more traditional wedding seasons of summer and fall? These are our top three reasons why couples are falling in love with spring ceremonies.

#1: Spring Wedding Weather Hype is Real

Couples looking to steer clear of winter weather—electing to forgo snow, low temperatures, and the potential for ice storms—may find that springtime presents an opportunity to experience cooler weather without the hassle. 

While forecasts tend to vary by location and timing within the season, spring weddings can offer a middle ground between scorching heat and bitter cold, boasting ideal temperatures and sunshine with intermittent showers.

If you’re interested in hosting an outdoor or semi-outdoor celebration, opting for a March, April, or May date could offer the perfect flexibility for indoor-outdoor hybrid ceremonies, receptions, and photos.

After all, saying ‘I do’ under clear skies and gentle breezes—without sweating through their vows or worrying about snow—is nothing short of a dream.

#2: Experience Nature in Full Color

Spring weddings are a unique blend of nature, romance, and atmosphere, with the stark changes occurring over the season acting as a natural canvas for every event. When nature is alive and well and able to do the work for you, the amount of budget needed for decor can be significantly reduced. Instead, these funds can be invested in a special vendor or product, a creative guest engagement opportunity, or something entirely different.

While springtime is suitable for a vast range of aesthetics and themes, it is typically ideal for couples interested in floral-heavy themes, garden weddings, and light, airy aesthetics to lean into the season’s natural beauty—think cherry blossoms, daffodils, tulips, and wildflowers in full bloom backed by the vibrant green haze of newly opened leaves.

#3: Honor Your Love Story with Intentionality

Every couple’s journey is uniquely beautiful, but many of the most renowned romances are peppered with renewal and rebirth at every turn, the same type of transformations that springtime is known for.

Your love story is defined by so much more than one hectic yet brilliant day. Although it may sound obvious, at its core, weddings are all about celebrating two people and their commitment to each other through all chapters of life, not how long the guest list is, how extensive the budget might be, or what decor is used. 

Lean into the season’s sentiment and bring added intention to the day by utilizing it as a powerful symbol of starting anew together. Selecting a spring wedding date is another subtle yet outstanding way to remind yourselves that your marriage marks a new season, defined by growth, new life, and fresh starts.

Looking Ahead

If a spring wedding feels like the perfect fit for your love story, don’t wait—spring 2026 dates are filling up fast as couples begin planning their nuptials.

posts.title: Hang Up and Hang Out: The Popularity Rise of Couples Retreats

posts.body:
Many people long to get away from the hustle and bustle of everyday life, and what better way to do so than by going off the grid? Now is the time to hit pause on life and try your first couples retreat. A couples retreats offers dedicated time away from everyday distractions for partners to focus solely on their relationship.

Retreats may entail a weekend getaway focused on relaxation or lots of activities to strengthen and build your bond. There are five common types of couples retreats:

  • Therapeutic retreats: These are often led by licensed therapists or counselors and are designed to address specific issues within the relationship through individual and joint counseling, workshops, and exercises.
  • Wellness retreats: This type of retreat focuses on holistic healing, with activities that may include yoga, meditation, and spa treatments.
  • Adventure retreats: Get moving! These often include numerous outdoor activities, such as ziplining, hiking, or kayaking. 
  • Spiritual retreats: This type is centered on spiritual growth and connection and often includes prayer, meditation, and mindfulness.
  • Luxury retreats: An upscale getaway where you and your partner are catered to and have access to luxury amenities.

Popularity of Couples Retreats

Couples retreats are becoming increasingly popular because they offer dedicated time and space to slow down together. This time allows couples to focus on each other, whether it’s rekindling a sense of excitement, prioritizing communication, or simply enjoying each other’s presence. Couples retreat attendees reap benefits that a different type of vacation may not offer, such as the following.

A Break from Technology and Work

In today’s digital age, it is easy to become so engrossed in your phone or work that it becomes an extension of your entire personality. Working late hours or balancing opposite working schedules can put a strain on your relationship. Couples retreats enable you to disengage from the demands of everyday life and give undivided attention to your partner. 

In retreat settings, the use of technology is often limited. Studies have shown that technology can put a strain on relationships, leading to dissatisfaction and unhappiness. Stowing your phone and laptop away for a few days can help you form healthy habits that you can bring home and strengthen your relationship in the long term.

Renewing and Reviving Intimacy 

Retreats welcome couples at any stage of their relationship, whether they are newly married or approaching their 50th anniversary. Physical and emotional intimacy builds trust, deepens connections, and fosters a healthy relationship overall. 

Intimacy is an essential aspect of any relationship, as it allows you to learn about your partner in a much deeper, more personal way. Bodies produce a hormone called “oxytocin,” also known as the love hormone, which is released during physical and emotional intimate moments. Retreats can revive or strengthen this level of intimacy between two people.

Lost in Each Other 

Ready to find the perfect retreat for you and your partner? Here at The Valley Venues, we offer a luxury option:  “Lost in the Woods” is the ideal choice for a couples retreat or even for honeymooners ready to celebrate their marriage.

This luxury cabin is nestled away in the woods, offering privacy and beautiful scenery. The cabin is designed for romance and tranquility with a wide range of amenities, including but not limited to:

  • A private outdoor grilling, kitchen area, fire pit, and waterfall: Soak up the beauty of the night sky.

posts.title: Four Tips for Creating a Stunning Spring Wedding Palette
posts.standfirst: Explore how to get started creating a beautiful spring wedding palette that will match the season and your preferences perfectly.
posts.body:
As the weather changes from cold to warm, spring brings an abundance of new beginnings and stunning scenery that set a perfect backdrop for any wedding. In fact, spring is often considered the beginning of the wedding season. And despite a 2024 survey from The Knot finding that 42% of weddings took place between September and November in 2023, spring remains a very appealing time for couples to set their special day.

Whether it’s the mild weather or the draw of in-season springtime flowers, a wedding can’t even begin to get off the ground without putting together a spring wedding palette. Choosing colors for your wedding is the first step in the planning process, and it’s easy for it to feel overwhelming, especially if you want to create the perfect palette that suits your seasonal tastes. 

Here at The Valley Venues, we’re going to share some insider tips on how we help our clients create the stunning wedding palettes of their dreams. 

Consider the theme of your spring wedding

Color palettes can tie directly to the overall theme of your wedding, and your wedding theme can go a long way in helping you narrow down the color choices you have to pick from. Think of your wedding theme as a style guide—whether you’re leaning more modern, boho, rustic, elegant, or romantic, the theme provides a foundation on which to build.

For example, a beach-themed wedding might lean into colors like soft blue, white, green, and orange, which reflect the surrounding scenery, while a romantic-themed wedding might lean toward deep red, pink, and gold. Consider your theme as you think over colors.

Pull inspiration directly from spring colors 

A spring wedding color palette can be guided by the season itself. Spring is known for being a very colorful season, with seasonal flowers and greenery dotting the landscapes of venues like our Lookout Deck. Take inspiration from the season as you create your palette. 

Spring palettes tend to lean into lighter hues like soft pinks, baby blue, mint green, lavender, and pastels. And don’t forget about other natural-leaning colors like light browns and tans that can bring additional warmth into a spring wedding color palette.

Dig into established and trending wedding colors

If you feel stuck on what colors you’d like to see in your wedding, there’s no better way to find inspiration than checking out what wedding color palettes are long-established or currently trending for spring weddings. You can find popular, existing color palettes by checking out wedding publications like Brides, Southern Bride, The Knot, and Inside Weddings. Many of these magazines have online archives that make searching for spring wedding colors of years past easy.

If you want to explore current, trending wedding colors, the same publications are also great places to start. You can also work directly with our co-founder, Kobi Cummings, who also happens to be a Certified Wedding Planner, to explore on-trend wedding colors.

Keep the color palette to a small range

It’s tempting to go absolutely wild for your special day and choose a wide range of colors that you feel work best together. But a too-broad palette can lead to color mishaps. It’s best to narrow your color palette to a select few hues. A range of three to five colors is a good number to aim for to help ensure that your spring palette is cohesive. 

Too many colors can make your wedding look and feel inconsistent. But with a small range, you’ll have primary, secondary, and tertiary accent colors that create a beautiful, coordinated palette. 

Get started creating your spring wedding palette today

There are so many elements that tie into picking the best colors for your spring wedding. You’ll want to pick colors that complement each other and don’t clash with the wedding theme, all while keeping the wedding venue in mind. The tips we’ve shared above are a good starting point for creating a spring wedding palette that you’ll love both in the moment and years from now. 
Be sure to connect with The Valley Venues to learn more about the welcoming, inclusive venues we offer and how our in-house Certified Wedding Planner can help bring your color palette to life.

posts.title: Corporate Event Planning: When and Where to Host the Perfect Event
posts.standfirst: If you’re in charge of corporate event planning, we can help you determine the best time of year & ideal venue options for your events.
posts.body:
Corporate events are certainly nothing new, but several years past COVID-19 restrictions, they are having a resurgence in popularity. Not only because it’s finally easier to hold corporate events again but also because companies are putting increased emphasis on culture and their workplace environment, with a particular focus on making their employees feel seen and valued. And The Valley Venues is here for it—literally, as we have multiple stunning spaces to hold your events as well as an all-inclusive approach to make your corporate event planning seamless. But first things first, when should you plan your event, and what should you consider?

When Should You Have Your Corporate Event?

Timing is an important factor in any event’s success. The “best” time for your corporate event can vary depending on the nature of the event (retreat, holiday party, etc.), location and goals. Here are our pros and cons for each season.

Spring 

The time period between March and May is one of the most popular times to host corporate events.

Pros:

  • Weather: Mild temperatures and more sunshine are present in many locations, including our Wildwood, GA location near Chattanooga, which is perfect for both indoor and outdoor events.
  • Winter Hibernation Has Ended: As spring gets into swing, people are ready to get out and about and are more open to engaging in new activities.
  • Less Competition: Now that the big holidays are over, venues and services may be more available and less expensive unless everyone else has the same idea!

Cons:

  • School Breaks: Families may go on vacation during spring break or right after the school year ends, potentially making it harder to get employees to attend if they’re away with children.

Summer

The summer season of June through August has its share of pros and cons as well for corporate event planning.

Pros:

  • Great for Outdoor Activities: Summer is perfect for team-building exercises, conferences with outdoor networking events, or evening activities like BBQs and casual get-togethers.
  • Lower Cost: While certain areas experience higher demand for venues this time of year, which can drive up cost, in our region summer is the least expensive time of year, which makes The Valley Venues a great option!
  • Relaxed Vibe: In general, summertime has a more relaxed feel, so there’s less pressure for a formal event; laid-back and fun will work just fine.

Cons:

  • Vacations: Many employees take time off during the summer months, especially in July and August, so attendance might be lower.
  • Heat & Humidity: In some parts of the country, excessive heat and humidity can make it difficult to enjoy outdoor activities or to want to attend an outdoor event for a long duration.

Fall 

September through November are also busy months for corporate events.

Pros:

  • Weather: The weather is what makes the fall season a favorite for so many, temperatures are comfortable yet crisp, making it perfect for both indoor and outdoor events.
  • Vacation Season is Over: With summer vacations over, most employees are back in the office and focused on work, so they have more availability to attend.

Cons:

  • Back-to-School: Even though vacation season is over, now it’s time for back-to-school, which means families with children may be distracted or have a more difficult time attending with school and extracurricular activities filling the calendar.
  • Holiday Planning: As fall moves into the holiday season, employees could become preoccupied with holiday travel or work plans.

Winter 

December is one of the busiest times of year for most of us, however, January and February tend to slow down and could be ideal for corporate events.

Pros:

  • Holiday Themes: December provides an opportunity to integrate holiday celebrations into your corporate event planning, offering a festive atmosphere.
  • End-of-Year Celebrations: Depending on the type of corporate event you have in mind, this could be a great time for planning future strategies, setting goals or hosting events focused on reflection and recognition, like awards ceremonies.
  • Off-Peak Pricing: Many venues and services are less expensive in winter, as it’s generally a quieter time for corporate events, except for the holiday season, of course!

Cons:

  • Weather Challenges: Snow and cold weather can disrupt travel plans for corporate events and planning an outdoor event is impractical across much of the U.S. this time of year.
  • Holiday Conflicts: Many employees take time off around the holidays, and others may be busy with family obligations, impacting attendance. After the holiday season, employees may partied out, so to speak, which can also impact attendance.

An Ideal Venue Any Time of Year

The Valley Venues has four unique spaces that are perfect for hosting corporate events in any season.

If you are looking for an event space that perfectly encapsulates the beauty of nature with modern comforts, then The Deck is the perfect venue for you. Highlighting the stunning mountain scenery, with a breathtaking view overlooking The Valley, consider our Lookout Deck for:

  • Meetings
  • Luncheons
  • Training
  • Team building
  • Fundraisers
  • Galas

The Valley 

The Valley is nestled at the bottom of a stunning mountain backdrop and features acres of luscious greenery. This beautiful space is an ideal outdoor corporate event venue for:

  • Meetings
  • Luncheons
  • Retreat activities
  • Team Building

Davis Hall

If an indoor setting would work best for your needs, our amazing Davis Hall venue boasts a spacious main area with room for up to 250 attendees, an attached food-staging area and a state-of-the-art sound and lighting system for entertainment. It’s a space perfect for hosting:

  • Meetings

  • Training
  • Team building
  • Fundraisers
  • Galas

Corporate Event Planning Made Easy

posts.title: Get You Winter Wedding Inspiration Here
posts.standfirst: Winter wedding can be magical with a unique blend of cozy elegance & seasonal charm, here's our winter-inspired mood boards & color palettes!
posts.body:
When thinking about winter wedding, the obvious red and green color scheme may come to mind. However, if it’s off in shade and secondary colors, it may feel more like a holiday party than an elevated wedding theme. Bright fire truck red and emerald green can look a bit outdated and overwhelming, but it’s how you style it and adjust the shading to make it work. 

Any “true” primary or secondary color will be a bold choice with personality and make a statement, but in a monochromatic setting, it can fall flat. The look needs balance, highs and lows paired with shades lighter and darker, dimension from complimentary colors, and a variety of textures.

Here, Kobi Cummings, the co-owner, art director and Certified Wedding Planner at the Valley Venues, shares some of her mood boards using classic holiday colors to help you craft your theme and color scheme for your winter weddings.

Winter Weddings Mood Boards

A Pearl In Winter

Seasonal patterns and textures like velvet and satin bring an element of refined luxury to winter weddings, especially with a more simple color palette. Here is Cumming’s “A Pearl in Winter” mood board; it showcases only three colors: dark olive, black and white. Textures and finishes like shiny pearls, soft twinkle lights and gold accents perfectly complement this palette. And add an element of interesting details that will shine throughout winter wedding. Olive green is used in this instance as almost a monochromatic color palette with pops of black and white to balance it out. As opposed to a true green, a warmer-toned version can be used here to create a cozy and charming ambiance. As seen in Sofia Richie and Elliot Grainge’s wedding, the limited color palette gives a chic elegance that some have noted as “quiet luxury.”

Enchanted Forest

In this true monochromatic pallet presented by Cumming’s “Enchanted Forest” mood board, various shades of green are used to create levels and depth that exist in nature in various earth tones. Leaning into the forest theming, moodier versions of green are used here to create the mysterious fantasy. Using natural elements on this mood board will be key to achieving this look. Couples can even make it a fun date day by taking a walk outside and gathering their own pine cones and ornamental branches. Use them as table centerpieces and aisle decor for winter weddings, or get crafty with your finds and turn them into stunning foliage arches. Brides.com has great tips on how you can incorporate woodsy elements into your winter weddings here!

Berry Bejeweled

Emerald, amethyst, ruby, sapphire, and amber are rich and will bring a luxurious, bold statement to winter weddings. These gemstone colors can add depth to every space, from the ceremony to the reception, with hints of each hue throughout. Here, the double-split complementary color palette works as these are all within the dark, cool spectrum. In Cumming’s “Berry Bejeweled” mood board, candles, glass and florals are used to bring pops of color. Luckily, many dark-toned blooms are in season, and other seasonal elements like evergreen sprigs and berries can be used, too. Run the World actress Bresha Webb married her TV writer husband Nick Jones Jr. using the berry-hued tones in the florals of their nuptials, as shown in this People Magazine exclusive.

The Valley Venues is ready to bring your mood board to life! Whether it’s a winter wedding, summery celebration, or anything in between, Cummings and her curated planning and art direction can help you do it all. To learn more, contact us here!

There are a lot of moving parts when it comes to planning a wedding and many decisions to make to ensure the most perfect day. However, nothing is as stressful as day-of mishaps with your vendors. Selecting the right Chattanooga wedding vendors can be a daunting task, but making sure that you have a qualified team of professionals can help make the day as seamless as possible from beginning to end.

Luckily, as a warm, welcoming, and inclusive space to celebrate life’s most special moments, we’ve been able to vet some of the top Chattanooga wedding vendors, like floral designers, caterers, DJs and more. When working with The Valley Venues, we’re committed to ensuring you have an unforgettable day. As such, here are recommendations from our very own co-founder and Certified Wedding Planner, Kobi Cummings, on how to find the top vendors in the area. 

Florals Bring the Venue to Life

One of the most expected things to see at any wedding is flowers. They set the tone, convey the color scheme and add to the theming and style of the wedding. Outside of the beauty they bring, they are a deep-rooted tradition in a wedding, symbolizing blossoming love and new beginnings.

Florals adorn almost every aspect of the wedding, from decorating the ceremony, reception, bridal bouquets and groomsmen boutonniere. If anything were to go wrong, such as damaged or wilted blooms, wrong colors or out-of-season selections, it can transform spaces and remove personalized touches from an event that should specifically represent you as a couple. 

Kobi’s Tip: Find a vendor that can work within your vision and budget! Flowers can get expensive quickly so consider alternative options like using a faux florist! The quality of faux florals has come a long way. It is a fantastic way to save exponentially on your wedding for big-piece items, which are mostly seen from a distance, like arbors or photo walls. Some venues, like The Valley Venues, even have faux florals in the decor libraries. The couples can use them so they can save even more. You can also opt for a mix of fake and real flowers. Using live flowers for those closer-up details, such as bouquets and centerpieces.

Culinary Excellence for Every Palate

Catering plays a critical role in guest satisfaction because everyone remembers the food for better or for worse. Serving high-quality dishes, having variety, including options for those with dietary restrictions, and creative presentation can elevate the guest experience.

For many weddings, food helps create rhythm or flow, moving guests from the ceremony to the cocktail hour and then to the reception. If any portion of the appetizers or dishes gets delayed, it can throw off the whole timeline of the wedding day. Also, having enough food is absolutely essential. Making sure your guests are well-fed is key to a successful wedding—a hungry guest isn’t a happy guest so your caterer should guide you on an appropriate amount based on the size without upcharging you.

Kobi’s Tip: Get creative with it! You don’t have to stick to a couple of meats and sides. Consider the specific vibe of the wedding and how you as a couple can customize the food. If your first date was at a pizza restaurant, bringing in a brick pizza oven would be a fun and unexpected catering option. Guests also love interacting with food trucks. Hire your favorite local taco truck as the late-night snack option for tired guests as they leave the venue. In any option, look for a caterer who can provide a polished, all-inclusive service. This might include handling plates, napkins, and table settings, which ensures everything aligns with your vision. 

Capturing Every Precious Moment

Wedding photography and videography are tangible ways to document and capture authentic emotions and beautiful candid moments of your day. Ensuring you and your team are on the same page is important because they only have one shot (literally). If they show up at the wrong time or miss certain shots, this is one area where you can’t adjust or go back. It’s also important that you feel comfortable with the team(s) and that they are unobtrusive in capturing the day in a candid and natural way without getting in the way.

Kobi’s Tip: Before you book a photographer and videographer, ensure their work. Such as photo style and editing, aligns with your vision. Offer clear communication with them on what you want, preferences, special shots, and must-have moments. Make sure that they can deliver on those. It’s also important to build rapport with them. So you both feel comfortable collaborating on details, timing and any questions or concerns leading up to and during the day.

The most important tip is to take as much time as you need to make the best choice for the vendor that fits your vision. Make sure that they have the best intentions and that you aren’t just any other event that they’re doing that weekend but are dedicated to your day. After all your vendors are booked, make sure they are in touch and connected to your planner. On the day of the big event, the planner will be the one making sure all vendors are sticking to their timelines and that everything is organized. So it doesn’t put more stress on the venue or clients. Each aspect comes together to make this big day. You want to make sure that you have all these team players coming together and doing their part.  

Chattanooga wedding vendor research is much like dating; finding the right match for you may take a little time. Aligning your wants and needs with what potential vendors offer can create a lot of back and forth. But it’s well worth the extra time to ensure that last-minute problems don’t arise. posts.title: Elopement Made Easy: Five Tips for Planning a Day That’s All About You
posts.standfirst: Plan an intimate, low-key elopement at The Valley Venues. Here are some tips to help make your wedding day meaningful and exciting.
posts.body:
Elopements are no longer about running off to a courthouse in secret—they’ve become a deeply personal, romantic way for couples to celebrate their love on their terms. Whether you’re dreaming of exchanging vows on a scenic mountainside or keeping things simple with an intimate ceremony close to home, eloping offers an exciting and meaningful alternative to the traditional wedding. Here’s everything you need to know to plan the perfect elopement and how The Valley Venues can help you create a magical day.  

Why Couples Are Saying “Yes” to Elopements

Elopements are quickly becoming a popular choice for couples seeking a more intimate and less stressful way to celebrate their marriage.

From juggling guest lists and vendor contracts to figuring out seating arrangements, it’s easy to lose sight of what the day is really about—you and your partner. Here are some reasons why eloping has become the go-to option for many couples:

1. Less Stress, More Fun

    Traditional weddings come with a lot of moving parts, and that can be overwhelming. Eloping is a low-key option that lets you focus on each other instead of coordinating a big event. Think less about timelines and more about moments.

    2. More Intimate Moments

      For some couples, saying “I do” in front of hundreds of people isn’t appealing. Eloping allows you to have a quiet, meaningful ceremony with just the two of you (or a small group of loved ones), making it all about the connection you share.

      3. Budget-Friendly 

        Let’s face it, big weddings can be expensive. By eloping, you can save money and put those funds toward something else—like an unforgettable honeymoon or a down payment on your first home.

        4. An Adventure You’ll Never Forget

          Eloping isn’t just about getting married—it’s about doing it in a way that excites you. From a mountaintop at sunrise to a quiet garden surrounded by nature, your ceremony can take place anywhere you want. 

          The Perks of Eloping

          Besides keeping things simple, elopements offer some unique benefits that can make your wedding day even more special:

          • Ultimate Flexibility: No schedules, no timelines, no pressure. Elopements give you the freedom to design the day exactly how you want it. Want to get married at sunrise? Go for it! Want to plan a spontaneous post-ceremony road trip? The sky’s the limit.
          • Focus on the Experience: Without all the extra wedding-day obligations, eloping allows you to focus on the experience itself. You get to live in the moment, genuinely connecting with your partner. It’s less about the party and more about the meaning behind your vows.
          • The Perfect Excuse for a Celebration Later: Eloping doesn’t mean skipping out on celebrations with family and friends. Many couples who elope later plan a reception or party to share the joy with their loved ones. It’s the best of both worlds—you get your intimate ceremony and still have the option to throw a party when you’re ready.

          Five Tips for Planning the Perfect Elopement

          While eloping is simpler than a full-scale wedding, a bit of planning still goes a long way. Here are some tips to help you create a memorable elopement:

          1. Pick the Right Location.

            The beauty of eloping is the flexibility it offers. Think about places that have meaning to both of you—whether it’s the first spot you vacationed together or somewhere you’ve always dreamed of going. The Valley Venues, nestled in the scenic hills of Wildwood, Georgia, just outside of Chattanooga, Tennessee, offers stunning natural landscapes perfect for an intimate elopement, whether you’re dreaming of a rustic outdoor charm with all the modern amenities of world-class event space.

            2. Make it Legal.

              Even though eloping can feel carefree, don’t forget the legalities. Depending on where you elope, you might need a marriage license, and some locations have specific rules about who can officiate. Be sure to check local requirements beforehand to avoid any last-minute surprises.

              3. Add Personal Touches.

                One of the best parts of eloping is that you can make it 100% personal. Write your own vows, wear something non-traditional, or incorporate elements that reflect your relationship. It’s all about what feels right for you. Want to pop a bottle of champagne on a mountaintop or have a picnic after your ceremony? Do it!

                4. Capture the Moment.

                  Just because you’re eloping doesn’t mean you should skip out on documenting the day. Hire a photographer or videographer to capture all the sweet moments—you’ll want to relive them, and it’s a great way to share your day with loved ones later. Imagine the amazing pictures of you two against a backdrop of Tennessee’s rolling hills!

                  5. Plan a Celebration Later.

                    If you still want to celebrate with friends and family after your elopement, consider hosting a casual gathering or party when you return. This way, you get the best of both worlds—a private, personal wedding day and a chance to celebrate with loved ones afterward.

                    How The Valley Venues Can Make Your Elopement Special

                    At The Valley Venues, we understand your elopement should be as unique as your love story. That’s why we offer a variety of breathtaking locations perfect for an intimate ceremony. Whether you envision a rustic setting surrounded by nature at The Valley or a private indoor space with a cozy, romantic vibe, we’ve got you covered.Not only do we provide stunning backdrops, props, and accessories, but we also offer on-site lodging so you can celebrate without having to rush off. Our team is here to help with all the little details, ensuring your elopement is as stress-free as possible. Whether it’s helping you find an officiant, coordinating photography, or arranging a post-ceremony picnic, we’ve got everything you need to create a day filled with love and lasting memories. posts.title: Micro Weddings: When Less is More for Your Big Day
posts.standfirst: Discover the intimate and personalized charm of micro weddings. Learn why couples are embracing this trend and how The Valley Venues can make your dream wedding a reality.
posts.body:
Picture this: a breathtaking venue, an intimate gathering of your nearest and dearest, and a celebration as unique as your love story. Welcome to the world of micro weddings—a growing trend redefining how couples tie the knot. Personalization and authenticity matter. That’s why more and more couples are opting for smaller, more intimate affairs that allow them to focus on their commitment to each other and the joy of sharing this moment with their closest loved ones.

But what exactly is a micro wedding, and why are so many couples gravitating towards this alternative to the traditional grand affair? Is this smaller, more personalized wedding style the right fit for you and your partner? Here are the reasons behind their rising popularity, and here’s how The Valley Venues can provide the perfect backdrop for your intimate celebration of love. Get ready to discover a new way to say “I do”—one that prioritizes heartfelt moments, exquisite details, and the beauty of your unique love story.

What is a Micro Wedding?

A micro wedding is a scaled-down version of a traditional wedding, typically hosting 50 or fewer guests. These weddings maintain all the elements of a traditional ceremony and reception but on a much smaller scale, allowing for a more intimate and personalized celebration. Despite the smaller guest list, micro weddings are often no less elegant or meaningful. In fact, many couples find that a micro wedding allows them to focus on the finer details, invest in higher-quality experiences for their guests, and truly enjoy every moment of their special day.

The Rise of Micro Weddings

Micro weddings have become popular for several reasons, especially in recent years. One major factor is the shift in wedding priorities. Modern couples often focus more on creating a meaningful experience than hosting a large, elaborate event. By keeping the guest list small, they can spend more time with each attendee and create lasting memories without the stress of managing a massive celebration.

Additionally, the events of the past few years, such as the COVID-19 pandemic, have led many couples to reimagine what a wedding should look like. Restrictions on gatherings, social distancing measures, and safety concerns prompted a rise in smaller, more intimate weddings. Even as restrictions have eased, the appeal of micro weddings has remained strong.

Couples are also drawn to the financial benefits of hosting a micro wedding. With fewer guests to accommodate, couples can allocate more of their budget toward personalized details, such as high-quality catering, stunning floral arrangements, or a designer wedding gown, creating a truly bespoke event.

Why The Valley Venues?

For couples considering a micro wedding, finding the right venue is key to creating the perfect atmosphere. Nestled just outside Chattanooga, The Valley Venues offers a breathtaking backdrop for any micro wedding, elopement, or engagement photos. Set on a 74-acre pastoral property, The Valley Venues has four unique locales catering to various styles and preferences.

Here’s a closer look at each venue

The Magnolia House

This historic Greek revival mansion, surrounded by lush flowers and evergreens, is ideal for couples seeking a timeless, elegant setting. Whether it’s for an intimate ceremony or beautiful engagement photos, The Magnolia House exudes charm and sophistication.

The Lookout Deck

If panoramic views are on your wish list, the 15,000-square-foot wrap-around deck overlooking Lookout Mountain provides an unforgettable location. With breathtaking views, it’s perfect for intimate ceremonies and receptions with your closest family and friends.

The Valley

For couples who dream of a natural, serene setting, The Valley offers rolling fields, wildflowers, and creek-lined waterfronts. This picturesque location is ideal for romantic elopements or micro weddings that feel genuinely connected to nature.

Davis Hall

Looking for a more modern, sophisticated space? Davis Hall provides a chic indoor setting with all the amenities you need for a lively reception following your micro wedding ceremony. Its polished, contemporary design adds a touch of urban flair to your celebration.

Each locale at The Valley Venues offers a unique charm, ensuring that your wedding will reflect your personal style and vision. Whether you’re looking for a romantic outdoor ceremony or a cozy indoor celebration, The Valley Venues has something for everyone.

Tailored Experiences for Every Couple

At The Valley Venues, we understand that no two love stories are the same, and your wedding should be as unique as your relationship. That’s why we specialize in crafting experiences that cater to your preferences, ensuring your special day is everything you’ve dreamed of.

For couples opting for a micro wedding, The Valley Venues offers packages designed for up to 56 guests. With a 6-hour venue rental, access to our luxury getting-ready suites, and stunning décor options, we provide everything you need to create a beautiful, stress-free wedding day.

Our dedicated team of coordinators will work closely with you to personalize every detail, ensuring that your day runs smoothly from start to finish.

If you’re considering an even smaller celebration, we also offer elopement packages for couples who want to focus solely on each other. With a 2-hour venue rental, a choice of ceremony spaces, an onsite coordinator, and an arbor and floral package, our elopements are designed to be romantic, intimate, and stress-free.

For those looking to capture their love before the wedding, our venue is also available for engagement photo sessions. The Magnolia House, with its historic charm, or The Valley, with its natural beauty, provide stunning backdrops for engagement photos that will capture the essence of your relationship.

As more couples embrace the idea of smaller, personalized weddings, the trend of micro weddings continues to grow. Couples are discovering the joy of celebrating with their closest family and friends in an intimate setting that feels uniquely theirs. The Valley Venues offers the perfect combination of elegance, flexibility, and natural beauty, making it the ideal location for your micro wedding. Learn more about our micro wedding options today!

She met us over Labor Day weekend so we could tour the property and talk about the logistics. Kobi was kind, calming, and sympathetic to the situation the hotel had put us in. Valley Venues is a beautiful space and the outdoor views are breathtaking! The outdoor cocktail hour was perfect for my daughter’s “garden party” theme.

The deck/patio had plenty of space for 11 bistro tables, a bar, Clumpies ice cream cart and a lot of room for our guests to stroll. The Lodge was a beautiful space for the bride and her bridal party to stay the night before. The groom and groomsmen arrived the next day and spent the day in their space playing pool and relaxing. Our guests stayed at the Double Tree in downtown Chattanooga (also a wonderful vendor as they accommodated our out of town guests on short notice), and it was a short and easy drive to Valley Venues. If you want a wedding in Chattanooga, make an appointment to tour The Valley Venues!!
